description: GENERAL STATEMENT US Army Corps of Engineers, Portland District, Bonneville Lock and Dam are soliciting for the purchase and installation of blade seals for Powerhouse II Main Unit Kaplan turbines. The turbine runners are 5-bladed vertical axis Kaplans. The contractor will supply and install turbine blade seals on the Kaplan turbine of Main Unit 16. The second set of blade seals for Unit 17 is optional, as defined in this Performance Work Statement. The contractor will provide seals based on drawings and dimensions provided by the Government. The Government requests expedited fabrication, delivery, and installation at the earliest practicable opportunity following contract award. The Government anticipates contract award on or about 9/30/2026. This date is for planning purposes only and does not alter the Contractors performance obligations, which begin upon contract award. PERFORMANCE STANDARDS AND GUIDELINE REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, materials necessary to perform the work required under these specifications except for those items specifically identified as government provided. The Contractor shall place all trash and litter pickup in dumpsters located on the project. Telephone service will not be provided. The Contractor will furnish, deliver, and install newly manufactured Kaplan blade seals and all accessories at Bonneville Lock and Dam as detailed in this PWS. Contractor shall also provide required documentation as stated in section 5.1.3 of this PWS. Description of Supply and Service Supply Turbine Blade Seals. The Contractor is responsible for designing and fabricating one-piece solid seals for five-bladed Kaplan turbine runners. The seals are required to have redundant sealing edges, no split, and field-molded solid at site. No gluing, cold bonding, or hotbonding using additional material are permitted. The seals will need to be bonded without any external additional material (adhesive or elastomer) to ensure identical material properties across the entire seal and geometric continuity of the seal edges. The nominal packing size will have an OD of 45.252-inch and an ID of 43.993-inch. The blade seals are original to the 1980s installation and final seal dimensions are to be verified prior to delivery and installation. Approximate dimensions are provided herein for pricing purposes only. The seal housing (turbine hub bore and turbine blade trunnion sleeve) dimensions will be confirmed prior to the supplier coming to site for installation. For compatibility with material selection, the outer surface the seal will be against is cast steel. The inner surface of the blade seal housing is stainless steel. The seals shall be designed to fit within the existing packing box dimensions as shown on the supplied reference drawings: Drawing Description Number 330 - 5 X A Runner Hub Assy Sect 4296-JL-1 Follower (Seal Ring) 6532-T-2 Runner Hub Assy Plan 4296-JO-1 Runner Hub Assy Plan 4296-JM-1 Blade 6530-CR-1 Runner Hub 6529-BB-1 ** See solicitation document for more details **

title: PEO-FW Group 2 Air-Launched Effects (A2E) Assessment Event (AE)
description: PEO-FW Group 2 Air-Launched Effects (A2E) Assessment Event (AE) Submit NLT 25 September 2026 11:59 PM ET U.S. Citizens Only Purpose SOFWERX, in collaboration with the USSOCOM Program Executive Office Fixed Wing (PEO-FW), will host an Assessment Event (AE) to identify potential vendors to integrate existing compatible small, unmanned air system (sUAS) platforms into a Karman Systima Common Launch Tube (CLT). This event aims to accelerate capability insertion for platform systems to be quickly integrated into the CLT system for the purpose of launching Group 2 sUAS. Background/Synopsis The Adaptive Airborne Enterprise (A2E) is an interoperable system of systems designed to enable robust ISR capabilities through expendable, autonomous sUAS platforms, resilient data paths, and a common control architecture. FANTOM Core-enabled sUAS platforms are typically launched using the Karman Systima CLT system. Objective The objective of this assessment event is to gather information on the integration capabilities of TRL 5+ sUAS into the Karman Systima CLT for Air-Launched Effects (ALE). Specifically, the Government seeks to identify airframes capable of rapid integration into the Karman Systima Space & Defense CLT to support Find, Fix, Track, Target (F2T2) and Electronic Warfare (EW) missions under the Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) A2E program. Why You Should Participate USSOCOM seeks to enter into non-FAR or FAR-based agreements with Industry, Academic, and National Lab partners whose solutions are favorably evaluated by PEO-FW Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). title: Market Survey � Industry Insights on Industrialized Construction (IC) Methodologies for Army Installation Resilience
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This Special Notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes�it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). There is no commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation, make awards, or pay for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing responses to this notice. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Europe District (NAU) querying the commercial marketplace to gauge industry capabilities, technical maturity, commercial availability, and execution strategies regarding Industrialized Construction (IC) and alternative construction methodologies. The objective of this market survey is to obtain strategic industry feedback to operationalize recent Department of the Army policy directives aimed at accelerating infrastructure delivery, reducing initial capital costs, and increasing real property portfolio flexibility. 2. BACKGROUND & STRATEGIC INTENT In accordance with the Department of the Army Memorandum (Facility Construction Policy Implementing Installation Resilience through Industrialized Construction (IC) Methodologies), the Army is transforming how it plans, designs, and constructs facility assets. Traditional design-bid-build processes and on-site construction methods are too slow and costly to keep pace with modem operational requirements. The intent is to accelerate the delivery of critical infrastructure, reduce initial capital costs, and increase the flexibility of the Army's real property portfolio to meet rapidly evolving warfighter requirements. Historically, Army facilities have been engineered for 50-year lifespans, often becoming functionally obsolete before structurally deficient. Moving forward, facilities will be designed to optimize an approximately 25-year lifespan. This provides strategic agility to align with supported platforms and enables rapid recapitalization by allowing structures to be repurposed or relocated as missions change. As a result, the Army seeks to transition to modern Industrialized Construction methodologies targeting: 50% faster delivery timeline compared to traditional construction. 30% reduction in initial capital costs. Optimization for an approximate 25-year facility lifespan (moving away from traditional 50-year engineering baselines) to enable strategic agility, rapid recapitalization, repurposing, or relocation as operational missions evolve. 3. TOPICS OF INTEREST: IC METHODOLOGIES & FACILITY APPLICATIONS NAU is specifically seeking industry capabilities and technical feedback regarding five (5) primary alternative construction methodologies (Ref: ASA IE&E Memo, Para 3.a�e) as applied to three (3) key facility categories (Ref: ASA IE&E Memo, Para 5.a�c), though application to other repeatable facility types is also welcomed. A. Directed Alternative Construction Methodologies (Memo Para 3.a�e) Volumetric Modular Construction: Off-site manufactured three-dimensional volumetric units transported and assembled on-site. Kit of Parts (Panelized) / Pre-Cast Systems: Prefabricated components, wall panels, and structural assemblies designed for specific building configurations. Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB): Standardized, scalable steel structural systems. Tension Fabric Structures (TFS): Rapidly deployable aluminum or steel-framed engineered fabric structures. Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing): Automated, on-site or near-site concrete/composite 3D printing systems. B. Primary Target Facility Applications (Memo Para 5.a�c) Category 1: Aircraft Hangars (Para 5.a) Primary Focus: Application of Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) providing clear-span workspaces and environmental protection, erected in a fraction of traditional construction timelines. Category 2: Maintenance Facilities (Para 5.b) Primary Focus: Application of Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB) or Panelized Steel Structures capable of supporting heavy-duty overhead cranes while standardizing procurement and accelerating erection. Category 3: Barracks, Child Development Centers (CDCs), Kennels, & Repeatable Buildings (Para 5.c) Primary Focus: Application of Volumetric Modular Construction, Kit of Parts, or Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) offering high off-site quality control, enhanced thermal performance, and rapid occupancy turnaround. 4. CORE CAPABILITY & EXPERIENCE INQUIRIES ("THE PULSE") Interested sources are requested to provide clear, concise responses to the following core inquiries: Section A: Firm Overview & Strategic Alignment General Capability: Briefly describe your firm�s primary business model, technical focus, manufacturing capacity (if applicable), and experience operating as a prime contractor or key technology partner in Industrialized Construction. Target Scope & Capacity: What is your firm�s ideal project scale (e.g., square footage, dollar value, or unit volume per year) for delivering IC solutions? Section B: Technical Evaluation of Methodologies (Memo 3.a�e vs 5.a�c) Methodology Alignment: Detail your firm�s specific capabilities and execution track record in one or more of the following: -Volumetric Modular -Kit of Parts / Panelized Pre-Cast -Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB) -Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) -Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) Facility Application & Suitability: How well do your IC methodologies integrate with the designated facility types (Hangars, Maintenance Shops, Barracks/CDCs/Repeatable Structures)? What technical modifications or building code considerations are critical for DoD adoption? Are there other facility types that are not included in this announcement that your firm believes would be good candidates for IC methodologies? 25-Year Lifespan & Flexibility Optimization: With the Department of War�s stated objective of reducing the expected lifespan of these facilities to be constructed from 50 years to 25 years in order to achieve lower investment and maintenance costs, do you believe that the IC construction methodologies contemplated by this memorandum are viable delivery methods to meet the 25 year life span expectation? How do the IC methodology capabilities that your company possesses a 25-year optimized lifecycle? Discuss disassembly, relocation, structural repurposing, and recapitalization advantages of your system compared to traditional 50-year brick-and-mortar builds. Section C: Cost, Schedule, & Delivery Optimization Speed & Cost Metrics: How can your firm achieve or approach the Army's benchmark goals of 50% faster delivery and a 30% cost reduction? Supply Chain & Logistics: What are the key supply chain, manufacturing lead time, or transportation constraints associated with scaling your IC methodology across domestic (CONUS) and/or overseas (OCONUS) military installations? Contracting & Delivery Models: What project delivery models best support your manufacturing and installation workflows? Section D: Sourced Experience & Project History Provide up to three (3) representative project examples completed within the past five (5) years demonstrating successful implementation of IC methodologies. For each project, specify: Facility type and delivery methodology utilized (from Para 3.a�e). Timeline comparison (design/fabrication/erection time vs traditional estimated baseline). Cost performance and life-cycle/re-use features. Key lessons learned and recommendations for Government adoption. 5. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Firms possessing the capability, experience, and interest in supporting the Army's Industrialized Construction policy are invited to submit their responses in accordance with the following parameters: Response Parameters: Page Limit: Not to exceed ten (10) pages total (including cover page and attachments). Format: Microsoft Word (.docx) or Adobe PDF (.pdf) format, standard 12-pt font. Submittal Address: Submissions must be sent electronically via email to: Primary POC: andrew.a.cochran@usace.army.mil Secondary POC: ryan.s.shoemake

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following services: Title: Panic and Intrusion Alarm Replacement and Monitoring NAICS Code: 561621, Security Systems Services (except Locksmiths) Locations: Fairview VA Clinic, 1800 NE Market Drive, Fairview, OR 97024 Hillsboro VA Clinic,1925 NE Stucki Ave, 3rd and 4th Floor, Hillsboro, OR, 97006 West Linn VA Clinic, 1750 SW Blankenship Road, Suite 300, West Linn, OR 97068 The Dalles CBOC, 704 Veterans Drive, The Dalles, OR 97058 Bend CBOC, 2650 NE Courtney Drive, Bend, OR, 97701 Salem CBOC, 1750 McGilchrist Street SE, Salem, OR 97302 Tasks: Within 30 days, upon award of the contract, the contractor shall remove, install, and test all new components at each location. This should include, keypads, panels, motion sensors, and wireless panic alarms, to the quantity provided at each location. Motion sensors must be based off of PIR and/or Microwave Technology. Sensors should range in detection distance of 40 to 200 feet depending on the area being covered. Some areas will require 360-degree sensors due to cross areas. Sensors should comprise of anti-masking technology where available. Once installed, Contractor shall provide alarm monitoring 24/7. All Security Systems and components must have the ability to be live tested with the monitoring station every month. This will include individual panic alarms, motion sensors, door contacts, and any other form of input. All systems must have the ability to accept multiple access codes with only one master code. The system should have the ability to track which codes were used to arm and disarm the system. The system should have the capability to be armed and disarmed with the use of a proximity card or key fob. With the possible potential to use HSPD-12 compliant ID cards, commonly known as VA PIV Badges or CAC Cards. The government should have the ability to log into the systems remotely to arm, disarm, and view activity history remotely. Contractor shall reply to repair requests within 4 hours of call. All repairs must be completed within 5 days. If not the contractor needs to supply a detailed action plan and any mitigations Period of Performance: Estimate 12/1/2025-11/30/2026 plus Option Years 1-4. Potential candidates having the capabilities necessary to provide the above stated services are invited to respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to Danielle Carrico at Danielle.Carrico@va.gov no later than 9/26/2025 at 5PM PT. The Government will treat any information received as proprietary and will not share such information with other companies. Any organization responding to this Sources Sought Notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The United States Department Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), supported by the R8 Procurement and Property Support Services Division, Region 8 US Forest Service, CSA 11, intends to award on a single source basis. Purchase order type will be a Firm Fixed Price awarded to Alleghany Farm Services. This requirement is for the purchase of professional agricultural drainage construction services to install, repair, and improve subsurface drainage tile systems at the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), Plant Genetic Resources Unit located at 2862 County Road 6, Geneva, New York 14456. The work includes field surveying, installation of new drainage tile, connection to existing drainage infrastructure, installation of drainage outlets and rodent guards, and use of specialized equipment to install drainage tile within vineyard and specialty crop research fields. These improvements are needed to reduce waterlogged conditions, improve soil drainage and field access, increase the amount of usable agricultural land, and support plant genetic resource conservation, regeneration, and agricultural research activities conducted at the facility. This project is essential to support the mission of the United States Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service, Plant Genetic Resources Unit by ensuring that agricultural research and germplasm regeneration fields remain accessible, productive, and suitable for crop production. The installation and improvement of subsurface drainage systems will reduce standing water and waterlogged soil conditions that currently limit planting, cultivation, maintenance, and harvesting operations. If this project is completed, poorly drained areas will continue to experience excessive soil moisture, resulting in reduced field accessibility, delayed planting and harvest operations, increased soil compaction, and degraded growing conditions. These conditions will negatively impact germplasm regeneration activities, research trials, and field-based plant breeding programs by reducing crop establishment, increasing the risk of crop loss, and compromising the quality and reliability of research data. Failure to complete the drainage improvements will also reduce the amount of usable agricultural land available for research and regeneration activities, limiting the Plant Genetic Resources Unit's capacity to maintain, regenerate, and distribute plant genetic resources. Continued deterioration of drainage conditions may result in increased maintenance costs, additional crop losses, and long-term reductions in operational efficiency. The project is therefore mission essential to maintaining critical agricultural research infrastructure and supporting the conservation and utilization of plant genetic resources entrusted to the Agricultural Research Service.

description: Advance Procurement Notice Construction of Temporary Modular Workspaces Kingston, ON (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number:              87729 Approximate Estimate:      $20,000,000 Anticipated Posting:          October 2026 Delivery method:               Traditional (construction contract) Description:   The project comprises the furnishing of all labour, materials supply and installation of five prefabricated customized modular workspaces, fully fitted with washrooms, kitchenettes, offices, boardrooms, and furniture. Approximately 23,000 sq ft over 5 buildings. This work includes, but is not limited to: Prefabrication of building modules off site; Completion of civil works, site servicing and wood crib foundations to prepare the site for assembly and construction of modular office buildings; Delivery to site and assembly of prefabricated modules into temporary modular buildings; Tie-ins to existing utilities and the construction of a new access road on the site; and  Finish construction and outfitting of the modular office buildings on site. The solicitation process will start with a Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) as the first step of a two-step process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI. No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders will be invited to a site visit. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a bidder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a bid for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential bidders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 87729; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. To be eligible to participate in the tender phase, a Tenderer who does not hold a valid Designated Organization Verification (DOS) security clearance will be required to: Have submitted a response to the RFEOI. have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Tender phase (second step Tender Phase) as indicated in the Electronic Bidding System (MERX); meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the tender call (Tender phase) as indicated in the Electronic Bidding System (MERX); and has submitted a bid. DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. The contractor shall provide a fully mission-capable chase aircraft, along with a qualified pilot and observer crew, to accompany the RPA during all phases of flight outside of restricted airspace. This includes takeoff, traffic pattern operations, transit along established routes, and recovery. The chase crew is responsible for uninterrupted visual scanning, collision avoidance, maintaining communication with both the RPA and Air Traffic Control (ATC), Contractor-Furnished Aircraft & Equipment Requirements Performance: Capable of a sustained speed of 150 knots true airspeed at an altitude of 12,000 feet and below. Communication: Equipped with radios capable of communicating on two separate frequencies simultaneously (one for RPA inter-plane, one for ATC). Insurance & Liability: All chase aircraft shall be fully insured. The Contractor is solely responsible for damages to the aircraft or personnel. Absent Government negligence, the Government shall not be held liable for any damages sustained by the contractor. Onboard Equipment: Chase and RPA will operate beacons and strobe lights during both day and night operations. General Flight Operations Takeoff & Transit: The chase aircraft shall be overhead March ARB (KRIV) at the scheduled RPA takeoff time. The chase will accompany the RPA during pattern operations and transit to restricted airspace (R-2515 or R-2503) per the current COA and LOA. After drop-off, the chase will return to base and remain on standby. Recovery: The chase aircraft will report to the designated pick-up point (R-2515 or R-2503) 10 minutes prior to the scheduled handover time and orbit. Upon clearance, the chase will rejoin the RPA and escort it back to KRIV, remaining in formation until the RPA completes a full-stop landing. Transfer of Control: The chase will maintain visual responsibility until the RPA enters the KRIV traffic pattern and a ground observer officially takes over visual responsibilities. Any changes or substitutions require prior written approval from the Ordering Officer. Resumes for all personnel must be submitted to the Government. Chase Observer: Responsible for clearing for traffic and advising the RPA of potential conflicts or deteriorating weather. Possess a current airman medical certificate (FAA Class 2 or military equivalent) per 14 CFR 67. Must be current per 14 CFR 61.56 (Flight Review) and 61.57 (Recent Flight Experience). Shall comply with 14 CFR 91.17 regarding alcohol and drug use. Observer Qualifications: Must have a comprehensive understanding of federal aviation regulations for the operational airspace. title: Germany – Fibre-optic connections – Glasfaser
description: Zur Verbesserung der Wohnqualität sowie zur Steigerung der Attraktivität für die Studierenden sollen die Wohnanlagen mit modernen Glasfaser-Internet Anbindungen versehen werden. Zudem soll ein hochverfügbarer und performanter WLAN-Zugang für die Wohneinheiten sowie Teile der gemeinschaftlich genutzten Bereiche eingerichtet werden. Mit dieser Beschaffungsmaßnahme soll ein Auftragnehmer (nachfolgend "Auftragnehmer" genannt) für den Internet-Service der Wohnanlagen des Auftraggebers ausgewählt werden. Der ausgeschriebene Leistungsumfang umfasst die Lieferung, Installation und betriebsbereite Übergabe einer Gesamtlösung, bestehend aus WLAN-Komponenten, aktiven LAN-Switches, Endgeräten (Routern), sowie Breitband-Internet-Zugängen auf Basis von symmetrischen Glasfaseranbindungen. Nach erfolgreicher Inbetriebnahme übernimmt der Auftragnehmer den Betrieb des Internet-Services für sämtliche Wohnanlagen und stellt während der gesamten Vertragslaufzeit die Verfügbarkeit sowie die einwandfreie Funktionalität der Dienste und Infrastruktur sicher. Hierzu zählt auch die Instandhaltung der passiven Netzwerkinfrastruktur. Die Bereitstellung des Dienstes erfolgt abschnittsweise ab dem 1. Januar 2027. Es ist geplant, die letzte Wohnanlage im Jahr 2030 in Betrieb zu nehmen. Mit Inbetriebsetzung des ersten Standorts beginnt die Laufzeit des Gesamtvertrages, welche automatisch nach Ablauf von 10 Jahren endet. Da der Roll-Out auch von Umbau- und Modernisierungsarbeiten innerhalb der Wohnanlagen abhängt, erfolgt die Umsetzung des Auftrags sukzessive. Die geplanten Inbetriebnahmezeitpunkte für die einzelnen Wohnanlagen können der Standortübersicht in der Anlage Preismatrix entnommen werden. Zu den Einzelheiten der des Vergabegegenstands wird auf die Leistungsbeschreibung verwiesen. Es wird ein Vertrag nach dem Muster des EVB-IT Systemvertrag geschlossen.
